content.text: From spectacles that help us see to cameras that capture memories, lenses are everywhere in our lives. A lens bends light through refraction, allowing us to form images, magnify objects, and correct vision problems. Understanding how lenses work is essential for optics and many technologies.
is a transparent object (usually glass or plastic) with curved surfaces that refracts light to form an image.
Light bends when entering and leaving the lens
The shape of the lens determines how light is bent
Two main types: converging and diverging
Thicker in the middle than at the edges
Brings parallel light rays to a focus (converges them)
Can form real or virtual images

content.text: A converging lens is thicker in the middle and brings parallel rays to a real focal point. A diverging lens is thinner in the middle and spreads parallel rays apart so they appear to come from a virtual focal point.

In short-sighted eyes, the lens converges light too strongly
, forming the image in front of the retina. A diverging lens spreads the light rays slightly before they enter the eye, so the eye's lens brings them to focus exactly on the retina. (reasoning)
